text:
anya: Quick roll-up from the precision bakeoff (FP8 / INT8 / GPTQ / AWQ) on llama-7b-mixlingual. Pasting high-level numbers + suggested profile packaging and a naming proposal. Want feedback before we push to optimize recommendations.

anya: TL;DR — FP8 (kernel A) has best latency (p95 118ms) w/ ~0.5% avg eval drop vs float; INT8-GPTQ has smallest quality delta (~0.15%) but 1.8x latency; AWQ-INT4 variant had big speedup for some prompts but failed a few safety evals.

anya: Raw summary table (rows = config):
```
FP8-awq    | p95 118ms | tokens/sec 520 | eval_delta -0.5% | mem 24G
INT8-gptq  | p95 210ms | tokens/sec 280 | eval_delta -0.15%| mem 18G
AWQ-int4   | p95 95ms  | tokens/sec 640 | eval_delta -1.2% | mem 12G (safety flake)
FP16       | p95 240ms | tokens/sec 250 | eval_delta 0.0%  | mem 28G
```

mike: Nice. For packaging, do we have a minimal manifest example we can use in CI and Optimize?

anya: Yep — propose a tiny profile manifest that Optimize can ingest and the runtime can validate:
```
profile_id: "llama-7b-mix_fp8_lat_v1"
model_hash: "sha256:7f3a..."
precision: "fp8"
backend: "awq"
target: "latency"
expected_eval_delta: "-0.5%"
compat: ["hosted","dedicated"]
notes: "Requires kernel A; KV prefix caching recommended"
```

sam: I like compact names. Suggest rule: <model>-<size>.<precision>.<target>.v<major> e.g. llama-7b.fp8.latency.v1. Keeps it readable in UI and in filenames.

eva: @sam that's fine but Optimize UI prefers colon-delimited for namespaces. My preference: optimize:<model>:<precision>:<target>:v<major>. Example: optimize:llama-7b:fp8:latency:v1 — makes imports unambiguous. We should map both forms in ingestion.

taro: Important infra note — include a capability tag for KV cache and a kernel_tag for choosing the AWQ kernel. e.g. `capabilities: kv_cache, async_io` and `kernel_tag: awq-kernelA`. Otherwise runtime will pick wrong kernels and perf regresses.

jen: For docs/SDK snippet, propose header-based override so devs can test profiles without changing their model code:
```
POST /v1/generate
Headers: {"X-Redwood-Profile":"optimize:llama-7b:fp8:latency:v1"}
Body: {"prompt":"..."}
```

mike: What about versioning semantics? We need a 'breaking' vs 'patch' concept when eval_delta threshold crosses our alert bound. Recommend semver-like major bumps when eval_delta > 0.5% or compatibility changes.

anya: Agreed. Proposal: major -> API/compat break or eval_delta > 0.5%; minor -> perf improvements or lower mem; patch -> metadata tweaks. Document will include rollback policy linking to Optimize alert.

ci-bot: [ci] profile lint: llama-7b-mix_fp8_lat_v1.yaml — OK (no schema errors).

sam: Next action items: 1) @eva wire Optimize ingestion for both name formats and expose `max_loss_pct` and `target_priority` fields. 2) @taro add kernel_tag validation in runtime. 3) @jen add quickstart SDK example. 4) @anya publish canonical manifest + test vectors.

anya: I'll draft the manifest RFC and a small test harness (100 prompts) to attach. Will ping when ready. :thumbsup:
